newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian court says no crime to call someone gay.
newsitem.headline: Italian court says no crime to call someone gay.

text.p: An Italian court threw out a lawsuit brought by an amateur women's soccer team over allegations that they were lesbians, ruling that it was no crime to call someone homosexual, L'Unita newspaper reported on Thursday.

The case related to chairman Michele De Caminata's decision, reported by Milan newspaper Il Giorno in January 1995, to close down the "Brescia Blues" club because he said the women were letting lesbian sex get in the way of sport.
The players responded with a lawsuit for alleged defamation but the court ruled that to call someone homosexual was not a slur, regardless of a person's sexual preference.

"The idea that attributing homosexuality to someone is an insult to the honour, in the sense of an assault on the dignity of their person, must be rejected decisively," L'Unita quoted judge Luca Pistorelli as saying in his ruling.
"In other words, calling someone homosexual cannot constitute in itself a diminishment of the person."

Sociologists say Roman Catholic Italy tends to cover up cases of homosexuality. Few gays "come out" publicly and homosexuality is popularly considered a marginal practice, confined to artistic or bohemian people.
The judge upbraided De Caminata and Il Giorno for bad taste, saying privacy should be respected whatever a person's sexual orientation, but ruled that they had not committed an offence.
